message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that involves careful planning, safety precautions, and specialized equipment. While the tower’s routine maintenance schedule paints it every seven years, the actual painting process typically takes **about two weeks** (roughly 10–14 days) when performed by the dedicated crew of the Société d’Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel.

If you’re imagining a fresh, one‑time repaint from scratch—perhaps after a major restoration or a complete overhaul—the timeline could stretch to **one to two months**. That accounts for:

| Phase | Approximate Duration |
|-------|----------------------|
| Preparation & scaffolding setup | 1–2 weeks |
| Surface cleaning & priming | 1–2 weeks |
| Application of protective coatings | 1–2 weeks |
| Final inspection & touch‑ups | 1 week |

These estimates assume a single crew working continuously, which is rarely the case in practice. In reality, crews often work in shifts, and weather conditions can add delays. Nonetheless, the two‑week figure is the standard benchmark for the tower’s regular repainting cycle.
